from pathlib import Path
import glob, os, re

inputs_dir = Path('/inputs')
work_readme = Path('/work/README.md')
source_readme = inputs_dir / 'README.md'

prefix = source_readme.read_bytes()  # preserve byte-for-byte

# Discover matching files (basenames), lexicographically sorted
matches = sorted(Path(p).name for p in glob.glob(str(inputs_dir / '*-*.md')) if Path(p).is_file())

rows = []
for name in matches:
    p = inputs_dir / name
    text = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    title = None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith('# '):
            title = line[2:].strip()
            break
    if title is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f'No level-one heading found in {name}')
    rows.append(f'| [{name}](../inputs/{name}) | .md | {title} |\n')

append = (
    '\n'
    '## Reference index\n'
    '\n'
    '| File | Type | Description |\n'
    '| --- | --- | --- |\n'
    + ''.join(rows)
).encode('utf-8')

output = prefix + append
work_readme.write_bytes(output)

# Validation checks
written = work_readme.read_bytes()
assert written == output
assert written.startswith(prefix)
assert written.endswith(b'\n')

# Ensure no extra content after last row newline by reconstructing exact expected bytes
expected = prefix + append
assert written == expected

# Confirm links resolve and rows count matches files
for name in matches:
    resolved = (work_readme.parent / ('../inputs/' + name)).resolve()
    assert resolved == (inputs_dir / name).resolve(), (name, resolved, (inputs_dir/name).resolve())

print('Updated /work/README.md')
print('Rows:', len(rows))
print('Files:', matches)
